ItemReplicationManager.note: these are the level-instance spawn entry points. They take a `pItemData` this package cannot build for an arbitrary authored resource, and they spawn a world object rather than moving one out of a backpack, so they are not the drop path. Nothing in this class is named WantPickupItem or WantDropItem; the pickup side is the synced state machine below.

drop.conclusion: the game's drop is `validate the point, then remove the item from the backpack`. No world entity is created for the dropped item, which is why the catalog's `dropped` port and the `container_policy` parameter have nothing behind them in this build.

WantToDropItem(SNet_Player, pItemData, V.note: the packet the client sends; its sibling WantToDropItem_Local (0x175D430) is the local path. Neither is used by this slice: the host's own body is OnWantToDropItem, and the adapter writes only what a plan asked for.

MasterRemoveItem(Item, PlayerBackpack) /.decoded: both send m_removeItemPacket through 0x1768AC0 and then call RemoveItem; they take an `Item` instance, and the world instance of a backpack item is exactly what a stale reference would hand out, so this slice does not use them

PlayerBackpackManager.EquipLocalGear(GearIDRange) / EquipSyncGear(InventorySlot, GearIDRange, ...) build equipment from a gear range instead of switching to something already held, and that gear range is the `gear-block` binding this package does not own

transfer.conclusion: not implemented: depends on a transaction
evidence: the two halves are two different packets with two different payloads: MasterAddItem sends m_addItemPacket, TryMasterRemovePocketItemWithID and MasterRemoveItem send m_removeItemPacket
each body sends before it applies, so a failure between the two calls leaves the amount in one backpack or in neither and the caller cannot tell which
no body in this build removes from one backpack and adds to another in one packet; PlayerBackpackManager has no such method, and the two packet types carry one owner each
transfer.portRefusals: the catalog's `replacement_policy` on `equip` and `ammo_policy` are the same kind of promise: neither has a native destination, so neither row is declared at all

resourceIdentity.problem: every one of the seven rows names an item, and none of the three implementable ones can turn an authored `forge.resource.item` into the game's own number without a binding that does not exist yet
resourceIdentity.nativeNumber: pItemData.itemID_gearCRC, which is ItemDataBlock.persistentID for a non-gear item and a gear CRC for a gear (the same itemID_gearCRC ambiguity w1-native-world-paths.json already records)
resourceIdentity.existingBinding: ForgeWeapon already turns a gear instance into `GearIDRange.PlayfabItemInstanceId` (EquipmentNativeAdapter.GearBlock), which is the instance's own record, not a persistent id from a resource
resourceIdentity.missingHalf: RuntimeModule.ResourceProviders / RuntimeQuerySession.TryResource — batch C of %TEMP%\rabi-audit\implementation-plan.md, whose `ResourceRef = (string ResourceKind, string ResourceId)` is the interface this slice's ItemResolver is a narrowing of
resourceIdentity.behaviourUntilThen: the three handlers refuse the whole command with `item-resource-unresolved` (code) / ItemResolver returning false; no id is guessed from a name, an index or a checksum

playerIdentity.problem: the adapter must hand the game's own backpack lookup the `SNet_Player` behind a `gtfo.player` reference
playerIdentity.nativeDirection: the kernel's entity tables are one-way: `ResolveEntityInstance(kind, nativeObject)` answers the reference, and there is no public entry that answers the native object for a reference in this build (RuntimeKernel.Entities.cs has ResolveEntityInstance and ResolveEntity, both keyed by the native object)
playerIdentity.newerCode: the framework source now carries `public EntityReference? ResolveEntity(object instance)`; batch C's plan adds the object-resolver list that would make a reference-to-object answer possible, and the compiled framework assembly under ForgeRuntime/Framework/bin/Release does not have ResolveEntity yet, so this slice does not call it
playerIdentity.behaviourUntilThen: the adapter takes an injected PlayerLookup; a reference this environment cannot name is refused as `stale-or-unsupported-recipient`

replicationChecks.give: MasterAddItem's non-bot branch is the packet send, so a host call is replicated; the bot branch is local, which is correct for a bot whose backpack no client mirrors
replicationChecks.consume: TryMasterRemovePocketItemWithID sends m_removeItemPacket before it applies locally
replicationChecks.drop: the drop's own removal goes through MasterRemoveItem, which sends m_removeItemPacket
replicationChecks.pickup: n/a — no host entry point exists

gatesUsedByTheAdapter.authority: SNet.IsMaster plus the kernel's Ready state and IsHost, the same gate the equipment writes and forge.action.combat.mark use; the native bodies themselves do not test it
gatesUsedByTheAdapter.identity: the recipient reference must be `gtfo.player:…`, must be current in the kernel, must be nameable by the injected lookup, and the backpack's own Owner must resolve back to the same reference
gatesUsedByTheAdapter.world: the kernel's world epoch is the reference's epoch: a reference from another world fails IsEntityCurrent, so a stale plan cannot write into the new world

the non-host refusal and the not-game-master refusal, before any native call

the resource that cannot be bound, out-of-range quantity / count / charges, the occupied pocket slot, a backpack with no pocket slot

the native refusal path (a drop point the game refuses) and the three throwing-native paths as unknown commits
the result rows: one per recipient in the plan's order, the catalog's field names, target_count, and the aggregation of mixed runs
